findings.title: Deleting a client throws UnsupportedOperationException in FGAP V2 realms
findings.body: The ProviderEventListener registered in AdminPermissions.registerListener handles ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent by calling management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) (AdminPermissions.java line 91). When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled (which also enables the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature, so the new feature check in the listener passes), management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, whose clients() now returns ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). The exception propagates out of the event listener during the client-removal transaction, so deleting any client in a realm with FGAP V2 enabled fails with a server error. Additionally, because no V2 cleanup is implemented, the per-client authorization resources created in the admin-permissions resource server (via AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource) are never removed when a client is deleted, leaving orphan resources behind. setPermissionsEnabled should be implemented for V2 (removing the client resource and its permissions from the admin-permissions resource server) instead of throwing.

findings.title: canExchangeTo and management/permissions endpoints now throw UnsupportedOperationException under V2
findings.body: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but the token-exchange flow (StandardTokenExchangeProvider) invokes AdminPermissions.evaluator(session, realm, auth).clients().canExchangeTo(client, targetClient, token) for client-to-client exchanges. With FGAP V2 enabled this now resolves to ClientPermissionsV2, so every token exchange attempt produces a 500 instead of an allow/deny decision; before this change clients() returned the V1 implementation which evaluated or short-circuited normally. The same applies to the admin management/permissions endpoints (GET/PUT /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}/management/permissions), which call getPermissions, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, mapRolesPermission, mapRolesClientScopePermission, mapRolesCompositePermission, exchangeToPermission, isPermissionsEnabled and resource() — all of which now throw under V2. If these paths are intentionally unsupported in V2 they should fail with a controlled 4xx rather than propagating UnsupportedOperationException as a 500.

findings.title: Null 'Clients' type resource is dereferenced; existing V2 realms never get the new resource/scopes
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no per-client resource exists the code falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and immediately passes the result to authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without a null check. getResourceTypeResource returns null when the 'Clients' resource does not exist, and passing null into the JPA-backed findByResource throws, yielding a 500 on any client admin operation (view/manage/configure) for such realms. This is reachable because AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns early whenever realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null, so realms that initialized admin permissions before this change never receive the new 'Clients' resource or the new scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite) — no migration/backfill is provided in this PR. Either add a migration that creates the new schema objects for existing admin-permissions resource servers, or at minimum guard the null resource before calling findByResource.

findings.title: Unused imports, unused logger and dead code in ClientPermissionsV2
findings.body: ClientPermissionsV2 contains an unused static import of AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE (line 46) and an unused import of org.keycloak.authorization.model.Scope (line 27), which will fail Keycloak's checkstyle UnusedImports rule and break the build. The declared logger field is never used, and the private method getEvaluationContext (lines 262-272) is dead code that also solely justifies the ClientModelIdentity/DefaultEvaluationContext/EvaluationContext imports. Remove the unused imports, the logger and the dead method, or wire getEvaluationContext into the evaluation path if it was meant to be used.
